description: Analyzes The Color Purple through the distinct voices in Celie and Nettie’s letters, the recovery of concealed knowledge, Celie and Shug’s love, Sofia’s racialized punishment, economic independence, and changing spirituality. Examines missionary and colonial representation in the Olinka sections, debates over Black masculinity, and the limits of forgiveness and reunion.
